question: The Teesta low dam is located in which of the following states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Teesta Low Dam is situated in the state of **Sikkim**, India.
 
• It is located on the **Teesta River**, which is one of the major rivers in Sikkim.
 
• The dam is part of a hydroelectric project aimed at generating **hydropower** for the region.
 
• The project is crucial for meeting the energy needs of Sikkim and neighboring regions.
 
• The Teesta Low Dam Hydroelectric Project is managed by **NHPC Limited**, a Government of India enterprise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Teesta River:**

 
 
• The Teesta River originates from the **Tso Lhamo Lake** in North Sikkim.
 
• It flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before merging with the Brahmaputra River in Bangladesh.
 
• The river is vital for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric projects in the region.
 
 
 
• **Hydropower in Sikkim:**
 
 
• Sikkim has abundant water resources, making it an ideal location for hydroelectric projects.
 
• Hydropower is a major source of renewable energy in Sikkim, contributing significantly to the state's energy supply.
 
• Several hydropower projects, including the Teesta Low Dam, are operational in the state.
 
 
 
• **NHPC Limited:**
 
 
• NHPC Limited (National Hydroelectric Power Corporation) is a premier organization in India dedicated to the development of hydropower.
 
• It was incorporated in 1975 and has since been a key player in the hydroelectric sector.
 
• NHPC manages multiple hydroelectric projects across India, including the Teesta Low Dam.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim's Geography:**
 
 
• Sikkim is a mountainous state in northeastern India, known for its diverse terrain and scenic landscapes.
 
• It shares borders with Nepal to the west, Tibet to the north and northeast, Bhutan to the east, and West Bengal to the south.
 
• The state's topography makes it suitable for hydropower projects, which harness the energy of its fast-flowing rivers.
